ESP.landNote: No nationality limits on rural land; non-EU buyers need defence authorisation in some strategic zones (parts of islands, Ceuta/Melilla). Building on suelo rústico tightly limited.
ESP.entityNote: Asociación sin ánimo de lucro, Fundación or Cooperativa; foreigners with NIE may found; utilidad pública status and Ley 49/2002 tax regime available.
ESP.fundingNote: No restrictions on foreign donations; standard AML/transparency rules.

CHE.landNote: BGBB: farmland generally only for self-cultivating farmers, with price caps; Lex Koller limits non-resident foreigners. Building outside zones barely possible.
CHE.entityNote: Verein (no registration needed), Genossenschaft or Stiftung; foreigners may found; cantonal tax exemption for public-benefit bodies.

AUS.landNote: FIRB approval needed for agricultural land above A$15m cumulative and for vacant land; farmland registered with ATO; established homes banned to 2027.
AUS.entityNote: Incorporated association, company limited by guarantee or co-op; ACNC charity; strong precedent (Crystal Waters, multiple-occupancy zoning).
AUS.fundingNote: No restrictions; Foreign Influence Transparency Scheme covers political activity only.

PRT.landNote: No restrictions on foreign ownership of rural land; rústico land (RAN/REN zones) generally cannot be built on without licensing. Tamera precedent.
PRT.entityNote: Associação sem fins lucrativos, Fundação or Cooperativa; foreigners may be founders; 'Associação na Hora' fast-track; public-utility status possible.

NZL.landNote: Rural land over 5 ha is 'sensitive': OIO consent with benefit test and farmland advertising rules; 2025 reform eased business tests, not farmland.
NZL.entityNote: Incorporated society (2022 Act), charitable trust or co-op; foreigners may found; Charities Services registration.

ITA.landNote: EU buyers free; non-EU buyers subject to a reciprocity test. Neighbouring farmers hold prelazione agraria (pre-emption) on farmland sales.
ITA.entityNote: Associazione (APS/ODV), Fondazione or Cooperativa under the Third Sector Code (RUNTS register); foreigners may found; bureaucratic but proven (Damanhur).

JPN.landNote: No nationality limits, but farmland (nochi) needs Agricultural Committee permit and buyer must farm; forest/other land free. Foreign-buyer rules under review 2026.
JPN.entityNote: General incorporated association (ippan shadan hojin) via notary, or NPO hojin (prefecture approval ~4 months); foreigners may be directors.

DEU.landNote: No nationality limits, but farmland sales above ~1-2 ha (varies by Land) need Grundstückverkehrsgesetz approval; farmers may pre-empt. Außenbereich building restricted.
DEU.entityNote: Eingetragener Verein (e.V.), Genossenschaft (eG), gGmbH or Stiftung; foreigners may found; Gemeinnützigkeit tax status; strong precedent (Sieben Linden, ZEGG).

AUT.landNote: State Grundverkehrsgesetze: farm/forest purchases need authority approval, usually favouring active farmers; non-EU buyers need extra permit. Tyrol/Vorarlberg strictest.
AUT.entityNote: Verein (simple notification, ~4-6 weeks), Genossenschaft or Privatstiftung; foreigners may found; gemeinnützig tax status available.

FRA.landNote: No nationality limits, but SAFER can pre-empt farmland sales and 'contrôle des structures' governs farming use; PLU zoning limits new dwellings.
FRA.entityNote: Association loi 1901 (simple declaration), SCIC, SCI, fonds de dotation or fondation; foreigners may found; habitat participatif recognised (ALUR 2014).
FRA.fundingNote: No ban; since 2021 associations must declare foreign donations above about EUR 153k and the state may object.

DNK.landNote: Non-residents need Civilstyrelsen permit (rarely granted for non-EU); farm properties carry a 10-year residence duty (can be met by a tenant). Landzone building limited.
DNK.entityNote: Forening, andelsforening or almennyttig fond; foreigners may found; strong bofællesskab/økosamfund precedent (Svanholm, Christiania).

TWN.landNote: Land Act Art. 17: foreigners cannot acquire farmland, forest or fishery land; reciprocity for other land.
TWN.entityNote: Association or foundation (zaituan faren) needs ministry approval; foreigners may join.

NLD.landNote: No restrictions on foreign ownership; strict zoning (omgevingsplan) limits housing on agricultural land.
NLD.entityNote: Vereniging, Stichting or Coöperatie via notary; foreigners may found; ANBI public-benefit tax status.

GBR.landNote: No restrictions on foreign ownership; overseas companies must join the Register of Overseas Entities. Planning permission for rural dwellings is the real hurdle.
GBR.entityNote: Charity (CIO/CLG), Community Land Trust, co-op or Community Benefit Society; foreigners may be trustees; Findhorn and Lammas precedents.
GBR.fundingNote: No restrictions on foreign donations to charities (political donations excepted).

NOR.landNote: Konsesjonsloven: farm/forest property needs a concession (price control, possible residence/operating duty); no nationality bar.
NOR.entityNote: Forening, stiftelse or samvirkeforetak; foreigners may found; Frivillighetsregisteret; tax-exempt status.

USA.landNote: Most states impose no limits; about a dozen restrict nonresident aliens on farmland and many 2023-26 laws target 'foreign adversary' buyers. AFIDA reporting.
USA.entityNote: 501(c)(3) nonprofit, community land trust, housing co-op or LLC; foreigners may be directors; fast; deep precedent (Twin Oaks, Earthhaven).
USA.fundingNote: No restrictions on foreign donations to charities.

KOR.landNote: Foreigners may buy with report; farmland needs a Farmland Acquisition Qualification Certificate (must farm); permit zones for foreigners near Seoul since 2025.
KOR.entityNote: Non-profit corporation needs ministry approval; unincorporated associations easier; foreigners may participate.

CAN.landNote: Federal home-buyer ban (to 2027) covers urban areas only; provinces limit non-resident farmland (SK 10 ac, AB 20 ac, MB 40 ac, QC/PEI approval). BC/ON/Atlantic mostly open.
CAN.entityNote: Federal/provincial non-profit corporation, registered charity, housing co-op or CLT; foreign directors allowed in most provinces.

BEL.landNote: No nationality restrictions; tenant-farmer pre-emption on farmland; regional zoning plans limit building in agricultural areas.
BEL.entityNote: ASBL/VZW, fondation or cooperative (SC); foreigners may found; tax-deductible gift approval available.
BEL.fundingNote: No general restrictions on foreign donations.

HKG.landNote: All land is government leasehold; foreigners may buy, but large rural tracts are essentially unavailable.
HKG.entityNote: Company limited by guarantee with s.88 charity status; foreigners may be directors.
HKG.fundingNote: National Security Law era: foreign-linked groups face scrutiny.

ISL.landNote: Non-EEA buyers need ministry permission; reportedly since 2020 large acquisitions (land over ~50 ha or multiple properties) need ministerial approval.
ISL.entityNote: Félagasamtök (association) or sjálfseignarstofnun (self-owning foundation); foreigners may found.

SWE.landNote: No restrictions on foreign ownership of rural land; detaljplan and strandskydd rules limit building.
SWE.entityNote: Ideell förening, ekonomisk förening (co-op) or stiftelse; foreigners may found; quick registration.

GRC.landNote: EU buyers free; non-EU need a permit in border regions (Law 1892/1990), covering many islands and northern prefectures. Agricultural zoning limits building.
GRC.entityNote: Somateio (association: court registration, 20+ members) or civil non-profit company; slow courts; foreigners may found.
GRC.fundingNote: No general limits; NGOs working with migrants must join a special registry.

ISR.landNote: ~93% of land is state (ILA) land under 49/98-year leases; foreign acquisition needs approval. Kibbutz/moshav communities are a strong precedent.
ISR.entityNote: Amuta (non-profit association), easy registration; foreigners may found; public-benefit company possible.
ISR.fundingNote: 2016 law requires disclosure of foreign-state funding; 80% tax bill (2025) not enacted as of mid-2025.

FIN.landNote: Non-EU/EEA buyers need Ministry of Defence approval (since 2020); purchases by Russian nationals tightened. EU buyers unrestricted.
FIN.entityNote: Rekisteröity yhdistys, osuuskunta or säätiö; foreigners may found (some board residence rules).

LUX.landNote: No nationality restrictions, but rural land is scarce, very expensive and strictly zoned.
LUX.entityNote: ASBL or fondation; foreigners may found; public-utility status by decree.

IRL.landNote: No restrictions on foreign ownership of farmland (former Land Commission consent for non-EU buyers removed); rural one-off housing permission is strict.
IRL.entityNote: Company limited by guarantee (CLG) registered with the Charities Regulator, or co-operative; one EEA-resident director (or bond) required.
IRL.fundingNote: No restrictions on charity donations; foreign donations barred only for political purposes.

SMR.landNote: Non-residents reportedly need Congress of State authorisation to buy real estate; very little rural land.
SMR.entityNote: Associazione or fondazione; registration with state; foreign founders limited.

SYC.landNote: Non-Seychellois need ministerial sanction; moratorium lifted 2025 with SCR 10m minimum for dwellings; little land.
SYC.entityNote: Association (Registration of Associations Act) or foundation; foreigners may participate.

HRV.landNote: EU buyers free since July 2023; third-country nationals barred from agricultural land except reciprocity/inheritance; a Croatian-registered entity is the usual route.
HRV.entityNote: Udruga (association), zaklada (foundation) or zadruga (co-op); foreigners may found; registration ~30 days.

POL.landNote: Farmland plots over 1 ha generally only for individual farmers or with KOWR consent (2016 Act); non-EEA buyers also need Interior Ministry permit.
POL.entityNote: Stowarzyszenie or fundacja (KRS registration); foreigners may found foundations; OPP public-benefit status.

AND.landNote: Foreign buyers need government foreign-investment authorisation; very little rural land, much of it communal (comú).
AND.entityNote: Associació or fundació registered with the government; small jurisdiction.

CZE.landNote: No restrictions on foreign ownership of real estate including farmland.
CZE.entityNote: Spolek, ústav, nadace or družstvo via court register; foreigners may found.

CYP.landNote: Non-EU buyers need Council of Ministers permit, normally limited to one property of ~4,000 m2; large rural estates impractical. North under separate control.
CYP.entityNote: Association or foundation (Law 104(I)/2017) or company limited by guarantee; foreigners may found.

SVN.landNote: EU buyers free; non-EU by reciprocity. Farmland sales need administrative approval with a pre-emption order favouring farmers.
SVN.entityNote: Društvo (society), zavod (institute) or ustanova (foundation); foreigners may found.

BRB.landNote: Foreigners may buy; register with the Central Bank for exchange control.
BRB.entityNote: Non-profit company or registered charity under local Companies/Charities Acts; foreigners may be directors; small registries.

MUS.landNote: Non-citizens need EDB authorisation and buy only within approved schemes (PDS/IRS/Smart City); farmland generally unavailable.
MUS.entityNote: Association, foundation (Foundations Act 2012) or trust; foreigners may found.

SGP.landNote: No rural land; landed property needs approval under the Residential Property Act; state land on 99-year leases.
SGP.entityNote: Society or company limited by guarantee; IPC charity status.
SGP.fundingNote: Foreign Interference (Countermeasures) Act 2021; political/foreign donations disclosure.

BHS.landNote: International Persons Landholding Act: permit needed for more than 5 acres or multiple parcels.
BHS.entityNote: Non-profit company or registered charity under local Companies/Charities Acts; foreigners may be directors; small registries.

ATG.landNote: Non-citizen landholding licence required (fee reportedly ~5% of value).
ATG.entityNote: Non-profit company or registered charity under local Companies/Charities Acts; foreigners may be directors; small registries.

CRI.landNote: Foreigners may own land freely; only the coastal Maritime Zone is concession-based with foreign-ownership limits.
CRI.entityNote: Asociación (Ley 218), Fundación (Ley 5338) or cooperativa; foreigners may found; public-utility status by application.

ROU.landNote: Law 17/2014 (amended 2020): farmland outside towns goes through a pre-emption chain; otherwise buyers need 5 yrs Romanian domicile + farming. Non-EU by reciprocity.
ROU.entityNote: Asociație or fundație (OG 26/2000) via court; foreigners may found; public-utility status possible.

MAC.landNote: Land is state-owned and leased; tiny territory with no rural tracts.
MAC.entityNote: Associations registered with Identification Bureau; limited civic space.
MAC.fundingNote: No explicit ban, but political scrutiny of foreign links.

URY.landNote: No restrictions on foreign ownership; companies holding rural land must have registered (nominative) shares.
URY.entityNote: Asociación civil or fundación; personería jurídica from MEC can take many months.

TTO.landNote: Foreign Investment Act: licence needed above ~1 acre residential or ~5 acres commercial.
TTO.entityNote: Non-profit company or registered charity under local Companies/Charities Acts; foreigners may be directors; small registries.

ARG.landNote: DNU 70/2023 repealed Ley 26.737 caps on foreign rural land; repeal back in force after Oct 2026 Supreme Court ruling, but Congress may still void it.
ARG.entityNote: Asociación civil or fundación via IGJ/provincial registries; slow; foreigners may found.

BRN.landNote: Foreigners cannot own land; leasehold only with approval.
BRN.entityNote: Societies need government approval; very limited civic space.
BRN.fundingNote: Foreign funding subject to state control.

BGR.landNote: Foreign individuals generally cannot own land directly (EU citizens excepted); usual route is a Bulgarian company. Farmland rules for foreign-held firms unclear.
BGR.entityNote: Sdruzhenie (association) or fondatsia, public-benefit registration; foreigners may found.

EST.landNote: Agricultural/forest land over 10 ha: buyer needs recent farming record or local approval; non-EEA/OECD buyers need consent; border zones restricted.
EST.entityNote: MTÜ (non-profit association) or SA (foundation), online registration; foreigners/e-residents may found.

GRD.landNote: Alien Landholding licence required (fee reportedly ~10% of value).
GRD.entityNote: Non-profit company or registered charity under local Companies/Charities Acts; foreigners may be directors; small registries.

SVK.landNote: Act 140/2014: farmland must first be offered to local farmers; outside buyers generally need a Slovak farming record. Non-agricultural land unrestricted.
SVK.entityNote: Občianske združenie (civic association), nadácia or nezisková organizácia; foreigners may found.
SVK.fundingNote: 2025 donor-disclosure NGO amendment struck down by Constitutional Court (end-2025); political pressure on foreign-funded NGOs persists.

MYS.landNote: Foreign buyers need state consent and a minimum price (often RM1m+); Malay reserve and much agricultural land barred to foreigners.
MYS.entityNote: Society (ROS) or company limited by guarantee; foreign founders face extra checks.
MYS.fundingNote: No general ban; societies report funding.

CHL.landNote: Foreigners may buy rural land freely; nationals of neighbouring countries barred in border zones.
CHL.entityNote: Corporación or fundación under Law 20.500 via municipality; foreigners may found.

ARE.landNote: Foreigners own only in designated freehold zones; no agricultural land.
ARE.entityNote: Civil associations need ministry licence; founders must largely be citizens; no independent NGO sector.

MLT.landNote: Non-EU and non-resident buyers need AIP permit (usually one residence); rural land scarce and heavily protected.
MLT.entityNote: Voluntary organisation, foundation or association enrolled with the Commissioner for VOs; foreigners may found.
MLT.fundingNote: No restrictions; enrolled VOs must disclose donors.

BRA.landNote: Law 5.709/71: foreigners and foreign-controlled firms need INCRA approval and face area caps (e.g. 25% of a municipality); reform bill PL 2963/19 pending.
BRA.entityNote: Associação, Fundação or Cooperativa via cartório; foreigners may found; OSCIP/CEBAS status slow.
BRA.fundingNote: No restrictions on foreign donations; standard reporting.

MDV.landNote: Foreigners cannot own land (except mega-investment exception); leases up to 99 years.
MDV.entityNote: Associations registered with the state; restrictive associations law.
MDV.fundingNote: Foreign funding subject to government oversight.

MEX.landNote: Restricted zone (100 km borders/50 km coasts) only via bank fideicomiso; farmland only via Mexican firm with <=49% foreign 'T' shares; ejido land not sold to foreigners.
MEX.entityNote: Asociación Civil (A.C.) via notary; foreigners may be associates; 'donataria autorizada' status from SAT is bureaucratic.
MEX.fundingNote: No ban on foreign donations; donatarias face SAT reporting and spending rules.

ECU.landNote: Foreigners may own land except within 20 km of borders and other security zones (military authorisation); Galápagos special regime.
ECU.entityNote: Fundación or corporación approved by a ministry; 2025 Ley de Transparencia Social adds SEPS registration and risk-based reporting.
ECU.fundingNote: 2025 Ley de Transparencia Social: donor registry, fund freezes, suspensions; under court challenge.

BTN.landNote: Foreigners cannot own land in Bhutan.
BTN.entityNote: CSO Act: founders must be Bhutanese; CSO Authority approval.

CUB.landNote: Foreigners cannot own rural land; only state joint ventures.
CUB.entityNote: Associations need a state sponsor and approval.
CUB.fundingNote: Foreign funds tightly controlled; independent groups prosecuted.

THA.landNote: Foreigners cannot own land; leases capped at 30 years (2025 Supreme Court voided pre-agreed renewals); 99-year lease proposal stalled.
THA.entityNote: Thai foundation (mulanithi) or association; boards that are majority-foreign are treated as alien for land.
THA.fundingNote: Foreign funding allowed; draft NPO control bill not enacted.

LTU.landNote: Farmland only for EU/EEA/NATO/OECD nationals with 3 yrs farming experience or approval; 500 ha cap; neighbour pre-emption.
LTU.entityNote: Asociacija, viešoji įstaiga (VšĮ) or labdaros fondas; foreigners may found.

GEO.landNote: Constitution reserves agricultural land for citizens and Georgian firms without a dominant foreign owner; non-agricultural land open.
GEO.entityNote: NNLE registration is quick, but 2024 foreign-influence and 2025 FARA laws bring stigma and criminal penalties.
GEO.fundingNote: Foreign grants need government approval since 2025; a 2026 law criminalises unapproved foreign funding.

KNA.landNote: Alien Landholding licence required (fee reportedly ~10% of value).
KNA.entityNote: Non-profit company or registered charity under local Companies/Charities Acts; foreigners may be directors; small registries.

TUR.landNote: Foreign individuals capped at 30 ha nationwide and 10% of a district; military/security zones excluded; Turkish firms with foreign capital need permits.
TUR.entityNote: Dernek (association) or vakıf (foundation); foreign residents may found; heavy oversight under Law 7262 (2020).
TUR.fundingNote: Foreign funds must be notified to the Interior Ministry; 2020 law allows suspension of NGO boards.

PER.landNote: Foreigners have equal rights except within 50 km of borders (needs Supreme Decree).
PER.entityNote: Asociación civil or fundación registered with SUNARP; foreigners may found.
PER.fundingNote: 2025 Law 32301: APCI prior approval for foreign-funded projects; sanctions for 'improper use'.

HUN.landNote: 2013 Land Act: farmland only for registered farmers (Hungarian/EU), cap 300 ha; legal entities cannot buy farmland.
HUN.entityNote: Egyesület (association) or alapítvány (foundation) via court registration; foreigners may found; public-benefit status.
HUN.fundingNote: Sovereignty Protection Office (2023) probes foreign-funded groups; 2025 'transparency' bill postponed; post-2026 status unverified.

LCA.landNote: Aliens Landholding licence required for non-citizens.
LCA.entityNote: Non-profit company or registered charity under local Companies/Charities Acts; foreigners may be directors; small registries.

TON.landNote: All land vested in Crown/nobles; foreigners cannot own; leases up to 99 years with Cabinet consent.
TON.entityNote: Incorporated society or charitable trust under local law; foreigners may participate; small registries.

OMN.landNote: Foreigners own only in Integrated Tourism Complexes.
OMN.entityNote: Civil associations need ministry licence; founders must largely be citizens; no independent NGO sector.

WSM.landNote: ~80% customary land, leasable only with approval; freehold sales to foreigners need Head of State consent.
WSM.entityNote: Incorporated society or charitable trust under local law; foreigners may participate; small registries.

ARM.landNote: Constitution bars foreigners from owning land (buildings OK); Armenian-registered companies, even foreign-owned, can own land.
ARM.entityNote: Public organisation or foundation; foreigners may found; online registration.

SAU.landNote: Non-Saudi ownership limited to approved zones (new law effective 2026), excluding Makkah/Madinah; no farmland.
SAU.entityNote: Civil associations need ministry licence; founders must largely be citizens; no independent NGO sector.

VCT.landNote: Aliens Landholding licence required (fee reportedly ~10% of value).
VCT.entityNote: Non-profit company or registered charity under local Companies/Charities Acts; foreigners may be directors; small registries.

BHR.landNote: Foreigners own only in designated freehold areas.
BHR.entityNote: Civil associations need ministry licence; founders must largely be citizens; no independent NGO sector.

PLW.landNote: Constitution bars non-citizens from owning land; leases up to 99 years.
PLW.entityNote: Incorporated society or charitable trust under local law; foreigners may participate; small registries.

MCO.landNote: No rural land exists in this tiny urban state; buying apartments is otherwise open to foreigners.
MCO.entityNote: Association (Law 1.355) or fondation requiring sovereign authorisation.

DMA.landNote: Alien Landholding licence required (fee reportedly ~10% of value).
DMA.entityNote: Non-profit company or registered charity under local Companies/Charities Acts; foreigners may be directors; small registries.

QAT.landNote: Foreigners own only in designated zones; no rural land.
QAT.entityNote: Civil associations need ministry licence; founders must largely be citizens; no independent NGO sector.

LVA.landNote: Farmland buyers must be registered farmers, pass a local commission and (non-citizens) show Latvian language skills; 2,000 ha cap; non-residents excluded.
LVA.entityNote: Biedrība (association) or nodibinājums (foundation); foreigners may found; public-benefit status.

SUR.landNote: Most land is state domain granted as long-term lease (grondhuur); foreigners need extra permission.

IND.landNote: Non-resident foreigners cannot buy land; even OCIs/NRIs barred from farmland; state ceiling laws. Auroville exists only via a 1988 Act of Parliament.
IND.entityNote: Trust, society or Section 8 company; foreigners may be founders but face FCRA and security scrutiny.
IND.fundingNote: FCRA: prior registration, designated SBI account, no sub-granting; 2026 rules tighten further; 22k licences cancelled.

PAN.landNote: Foreigners may own land except within 10 km of borders; many rural parcels are possession rights (ROP), not titled.
PAN.entityNote: Asociación sin fines de lucro (MINGOB) or Fundación de Interés Privado; foreigners may found.

COL.landNote: No foreign ownership limits; former state 'baldío' land has UAF accumulation limits; foreign investment must be registered with the central bank.
COL.entityNote: ESAL: asociación, fundación or corporación via Cámara de Comercio; foreigners may found; Régimen Tributario Especial.

CHN.landNote: All land state/collective-owned; foreigners only get urban land-use rights; rural collective land off-limits.
CHN.entityNote: Social organisations need a state sponsor; Overseas NGO Law restricts foreign founders.
CHN.fundingNote: Overseas NGO Law: foreign funding only via registered/filed INGOs under police oversight.

VNM.landNote: All land owned by 'the people'; foreigners cannot hold farmland use rights; foreign firms lease from the state.
VNM.entityNote: Independent associations tightly controlled; foreign NGOs need registration.
VNM.fundingNote: Foreign aid needs state approval; environmental NGO leaders jailed.

LKA.landNote: Land (Restrictions on Alienation) Act bars foreign freehold; leases up to 99 years (lease tax abolished 2016); BOI projects may differ.
LKA.entityNote: Voluntary social service organisation (NGO Secretariat), trust or guarantee company; extra scrutiny.
LKA.fundingNote: Foreign funds to NGOs monitored by NGO Secretariat; restrictive NGO bill floated.

SEN.landNote: Rural land mostly national domain (not saleable); foreigners via leases (bail) or titled plots.
SEN.entityNote: Association by declaration (French-style law); NGO status needs a ministry agreement; foreigners may found.

XKX.landNote: Foreigners may own real estate; no specific farmland ban reported, but cadastre/ownership disputes are common.
XKX.entityNote: NGO (association or foundation) registered with the Ministry of Public Administration; foreigners may found.

VUT.landNote: Constitution: land belongs to custom owners; foreigners lease up to 75 years.
VUT.entityNote: Charitable association (Charitable Associations Act); foreigners may found.

MNE.landNote: Foreigners may buy buildings/construction land but not farmland, forests or border areas directly; a Montenegrin company is the usual route.
MNE.entityNote: NVO (association or foundation) registered with the ministry; foreigners may found.

ZAF.landNote: Foreigners may own freehold incl. farmland; Expropriation Act (signed 2025) adds uncertainty; proposed foreign farmland ban never enacted.
ZAF.entityNote: Non-profit company (NPC), trust or voluntary association; NPO registration; SARS PBO tax exemption; foreigners may found.

CPV.landNote: No restrictions on foreigners buying property.
CPV.entityNote: Associação or fundação; foreigners may found.

IDN.landNote: Freehold (Hak Milik) for citizens only; foreigners get Hak Pakai on residential land; PT PMA firms can hold HGB/HGU rights.
IDN.entityNote: Yayasan (foundation): foreigners may co-found with >=IDR 100m assets; at least one Indonesian manager; notary + ministry approval.
IDN.fundingNote: Foreign funds to local NGOs need government registration/approval; INGOs need MoU.

KWT.landNote: Non-GCC foreigners essentially cannot own land.
KWT.entityNote: Civil associations need ministry licence; founders must largely be citizens; no independent NGO sector.

BOL.landNote: Foreigners cannot own land within 50 km of borders nor receive state land; agrarian ceilings; tenure disputes.
BOL.entityNote: NGO legal personality requires alignment with state development plans (Law 351).
BOL.fundingNote: Decree 1597 lets the state revoke NGO status; foreign NGOs expelled in the past.

JAM.landNote: No restrictions on foreign ownership of land.
JAM.entityNote: Company limited by guarantee registered as a charity; foreigners may be directors.

RUS.landNote: Foreigners barred from owning agricultural land and border-area land; leases (up to 49 years) possible.
RUS.entityNote: NKO registration heavily scrutinised; foreign founders face extra checks and liquidation risk.
RUS.fundingNote: Foreign-agent and 'undesirable organisation' laws criminalise many foreign-funded groups.

BIH.landNote: Foreigners may own on reciprocity; farmland usually via a local company; rules differ between FBiH and Republika Srpska.
BIH.entityNote: Udruženje or fondacija at state or entity level; complex multi-level registration.
BIH.fundingNote: Republika Srpska adopted a 'foreign agents' NPO registry law (Feb 2025); Federation unrestricted.

DOM.landNote: Foreigners may own land without nationality restrictions; title (deslinde) verification essential.
DOM.entityNote: Asociación sin fines de lucro (Law 122-05); foreigners may found.

PRY.landNote: Free, except nationals of neighbouring countries barred from rural land within 50 km of borders (Law 2532/05).
PRY.entityNote: Asociación or fundación; Law 7363 (2024) adds a registry and annual reports.
PRY.fundingNote: Law 7363 (in force Oct 2025) requires registration/reporting of foreign-funded NGOs; constitutional challenges pending.

TZA.landNote: All land vested in the President; non-citizens only via TIC derivative rights for investment projects.
TZA.entityNote: NGO registration under NGO Act (2019 amendments tighten).
TZA.fundingNote: NGOs must disclose funding sources and agreements to the Registrar.

UZB.landNote: Agricultural land state-owned; foreigners only lease non-agricultural land.
UZB.entityNote: NNO registration is difficult and slow; foreign founders face restrictions.
UZB.fundingNote: Foreign grants need prior Ministry of Justice approval.

GTM.landNote: Foreigners may own land except within 15 km of borders; titling disputes and land conflicts common.
GTM.entityNote: Asociación or fundación; 2020 NGO law (Decreto 4-2020) lets the state cancel NGOs.
GTM.fundingNote: Decreto 4-2020 requires registration of foreign-funded NGOs and allows cancellation.

PHL.landNote: Constitution bars foreign land ownership (60% Filipino firms only); RA 12252 (2025) allows investor leases up to 99 years incl. agri/eco uses.
PHL.entityNote: Non-stock non-profit corporation with SEC; foreigners may be trustees for most purposes.
PHL.fundingNote: No general limits; SEC anti-terror-financing checks; red-tagging risk.

GHA.landNote: Non-citizens limited to leases of up to 50 years (Land Act 2020); customary land via chiefs.
GHA.entityNote: Company limited by guarantee plus NGO registration.

BLZ.landNote: Freehold open to foreigners; Aliens Landholding rules may require a licence for larger rural holdings.
BLZ.entityNote: Non-profit company or NGO registered under the NGO Act; foreigners may be directors.

FJI.landNote: ~87% iTaukei land leasable only (up to 99 yrs via TLTB); freehold (~8%) needs Land Sales Act consent for non-residents.
FJI.entityNote: Charitable trust or incorporated society; foreigners may found.

NPL.landNote: Foreigners cannot own land in Nepal.
NPL.entityNote: Local NGOs need Nepali founders; foreign NGOs need Social Welfare Council agreement.
NPL.fundingNote: Foreign funds need Social Welfare Council project approval.

KEN.landNote: Non-citizens hold leasehold (max 99 yrs) only; farmland deals with foreigners or foreign-owned firms void under Land Control Act.
KEN.entityNote: Trust, company limited by guarantee or PBO (PBO Act in force 2024); foreigners may found.
KEN.fundingNote: No legal cap on foreign funding; past 15% cap proposals defeated.

STP.landNote: Most land state-owned; access via aforamento/long lease.

MDA.landNote: Foreigners and companies with foreign capital barred from owning agricultural and forest land; leasing allowed.
MDA.entityNote: Asociație obștească, fundație or instituție privată; foreigners may found.

JOR.landNote: Foreigners need ministerial/Cabinet approval and reciprocity; agricultural land faces extra conditions.
JOR.entityNote: Society (Law 51/2008) via ministry; foreign membership limited.
JOR.fundingNote: Each foreign donation needs prior Cabinet approval.

GUY.landNote: Private titled land open to foreigners; much land is state land leased with government approval.
GUY.entityNote: Friendly society, company limited by guarantee or trust; foreigners may be directors.

LBN.landNote: Foreigners need a decree above 3,000 m2; foreign ownership capped at ~3% per district.
LBN.entityNote: Association by notification (1909 law); liberal regime; state dysfunction.

MKD.landNote: Foreigners may acquire construction land on reciprocity; agricultural land not directly (lease or Macedonian company).
MKD.entityNote: Association or foundation registered with Central Registry; foreigners may found.

MHL.entityNote: Incorporated society or charitable trust under local law; foreigners may participate; small registries.

ALB.landNote: Foreigners cannot buy agricultural land, forests or pastures; long leases (up to 99 years) allowed; buildings and their plots allowed.
ALB.entityNote: Shoqatë (association), fondacion or qendër via Tirana court; foreigners may found.

NIC.landNote: Private ownership allowed, but government has confiscated properties of dissidents and NGOs since 2018.
NIC.entityNote: Over 5,000 NGOs cancelled since 2018; registration effectively closed.
NIC.fundingNote: 2020 Foreign Agents Law and later rules effectively ban independent foreign-funded NGOs.

UKR.landNote: Foreigners and foreign-owned firms barred from farmland until a referendum (not held); 50 km border ban; war risk. Leases possible.
UKR.entityNote: Hromadska orhanizatsiia (NGO) or charitable foundation; foreigners may found; fast registration.

BWA.landNote: Tribal land reserved for citizens; freehold farmland to non-citizens needs ministerial consent (Land Control Act); state land leased.
BWA.entityNote: Society (Societies Act) or trust; foreigners may participate.

RWA.landNote: Foreigners receive long-term (emphyteutic) leases rather than freehold; clear cadastre.
RWA.entityNote: National NGO registration with RGB; must align with government plans; admin-cost caps.
RWA.fundingNote: Foreign-funded NGOs must spend most funds on programmes aligned with state priorities.

TUN.landNote: Foreigners barred from agricultural land; other purchases need governor permission.
TUN.entityNote: Association under Decree 88/2011 (declaration), but crackdown since 2023.
TUN.fundingNote: Foreign funding increasingly targeted; restrictive draft law.

KHM.landNote: Only Khmer citizens and 51%-Khmer firms own land; foreigners use registered long-term leases (up to 50 years).
KHM.entityNote: LANGO 2015: registration with Interior Ministry; political-neutrality duty.
KHM.fundingNote: LANGO requires reporting of foreign funds; arbitrary closures.

TUV.landNote: All land customary; foreigners lease only; tiny atolls.
TUV.entityNote: Incorporated society or charitable trust under local law; foreigners may participate; small registries.

SRB.landNote: Foreigners buy on reciprocity; agricultural land generally barred to foreigners (EU citizens only under strict residence/farming conditions).
SRB.entityNote: Udruženje (association) or fondacija via business registry, quick; foreigners may found.
SRB.fundingNote: No legal limit yet, but 2025 police raids on foreign-funded NGOs and a 'foreign agents' bill tabled in 2024.

ETH.landNote: All land state-owned; foreigners lease via investment permits.
ETH.entityNote: CSO Proclamation 2019 allows foreign founders, but the regulator suspended many CSOs in 2024-25.
ETH.fundingNote: 2019 law removed foreign-funding caps; 2025 draft amendments would curb governance funding.

CIV.landNote: Rural land ownership reserved for the state and Ivorian individuals; foreigners lease (emphyteutic).
CIV.entityNote: Association by declaration (French-style law); NGO status needs a ministry agreement; foreigners may found.

FSM.landNote: Non-citizens cannot own land; state-limited lease terms.
FSM.entityNote: Incorporated society or charitable trust under local law; foreigners may participate; small registries.

GAB.landNote: Foreigners may hold titled land with approvals; most land state domain.
GAB.entityNote: Association by declaration (French-style law); NGO status needs a ministry agreement; foreigners may found.

SLV.landNote: Foreigners may own rural land where their country grants reciprocity; rules otherwise liberal.
SLV.entityNote: Asociación or fundación registration slow; NGOs under heavy political pressure.
SLV.fundingNote: 2025 Foreign Agents Law: 30% tax on foreign donations, mandatory registration, heavy fines.

KAZ.landNote: Sale and lease of agricultural land to foreigners and firms with foreign participation banned (2021).
KAZ.entityNote: Public association or private foundation; foreign founders face residency limits.
KAZ.fundingNote: Recipients of foreign funds must report to a public registry; tax-authority scrutiny.

MAR.landNote: Foreign individuals barred from farmland outside urban perimeters; Law 62-19 (2021) lets SA companies with foreign shareholders buy with regional approval.
MAR.entityNote: Association (Dahir 1958) by declaration; foreigners may found; public-utility status rare.
MAR.fundingNote: Foreign funds must be declared to the Secretariat General within 30 days.

AZE.landNote: Foreigners cannot own land; leases only.
AZE.entityNote: NGO registration routinely refused; foreign founders face barriers.
AZE.fundingNote: Every foreign grant needs state registration; most foreign-funded NGOs shut since 2014.

NAM.landNote: Farmland sales to foreigners need ministerial consent (state pre-emption); 2025 Land Bill would ban foreign acquisition of commercial farmland.
NAM.entityNote: Not-for-gain (Section 21) company, trust or welfare organisation; foreigners may found.

COM.landNote: Customary and state land; foreigners via leases.
COM.entityNote: Association by declaration (French-style law); NGO status needs a ministry agreement; foreigners may found.

TLS.landNote: Constitution reserves land ownership to nationals; foreigners lease (reportedly up to 50 years).
TLS.entityNote: Non-profit association or foundation; registration with Ministry of Justice.

HND.landNote: Constitution bars foreigners from owning land within 40 km of borders and coasts (tourism exceptions); land titling weak.
HND.entityNote: Asociación civil or fundación via URSAC; slow procedures.
HND.fundingNote: No legal ban; NGOs subject to registration and AML reporting.

MNG.landNote: Constitution reserves land ownership to citizens; foreign-invested firms get possession/use rights for set terms.
MNG.entityNote: NGO registration with the State Registration Office; foreigners may participate.

BEN.landNote: Land code restricts rural acquisition by foreigners; leases common.
BEN.entityNote: Association by declaration (French-style law); NGO status needs a ministry agreement; foreigners may found.

IRN.landNote: Foreigners need permission to own property; non-Muslim and foreign ownership restricted.
IRN.fundingNote: Foreign funding treated as a security threat.

TKM.landNote: All land state-owned; foreigners have no secure tenure.
TKM.entityNote: Independent NGOs essentially impossible to register.
TKM.fundingNote: Foreign grants require state approval; closed civic space.

DZA.landNote: Foreigners barred from agricultural land; strict controls.

GNQ.landNote: Land under tight state control; foreigners need approvals.

KIR.landNote: Native land; foreigners lease only with government approval.
KIR.entityNote: Incorporated society or charitable trust under local law; foreigners may participate; small registries.

ZMB.landNote: Non-citizens may hold land only with presidential consent (investors/residents); 99-year leasehold.
ZMB.entityNote: NGO Act 2009 registration; periodic government reviews.
ZMB.fundingNote: No explicit ban; NGO Act gives broad oversight.

LAO.landNote: Foreigners cannot own land; state leases/concessions up to ~50 years.
LAO.entityNote: Associations under Decree 238 need extensive state approval.

BLR.landNote: Land largely state-owned; foreigners cannot own farmland; leases only; political risk extreme.
BLR.entityNote: NGO registration effectively closed; over 1,000 NGOs liquidated since 2021.
BLR.fundingNote: Foreign aid needs prior state registration; acting for unregistered groups is criminalised.

UGA.landNote: Non-citizens cannot hold freehold or mailo land; leasehold up to 99 years.
UGA.entityNote: NGO Act 2016: permits and district MoUs; 54 NGOs suspended in 2021.
UGA.fundingNote: Foreign-funded NGOs heavily scrutinised; accounts frozen in the past.

KGZ.landNote: Foreigners cannot own agricultural land; leases possible.
KGZ.entityNote: Registration possible, but 2024 'foreign representatives' law brings unannounced inspections.
KGZ.fundingNote: 2024 law: foreign-funded NGOs doing 'political activity' must register as foreign representatives.

MDG.landNote: Foreigners cannot own land directly; long leases or approved investment companies.
MDG.entityNote: Association by declaration (French-style law); NGO status needs a ministry agreement; foreigners may found.

PRK.landNote: No private land; foreign residence tightly controlled.

SWZ.landNote: Swazi Nation Land under chiefs; title-deed land needs Land Control Board consent for foreigners.
SWZ.entityNote: Company limited by guarantee or society; restrictive environment.
SWZ.fundingNote: Civic space restricted; few formal funding rules.

SLE.landNote: Provinces: customary land leasable (2022 laws allow ~50+21 yr leases); Western Area purchases limited for non-citizens.
SLE.entityNote: NGO registration and agreement with planning ministry.
SLE.fundingNote: NGO policy requires reporting of foreign funds.

SLB.landNote: Foreigners cannot hold perpetual estates; fixed-term estates (up to 75 yrs); customary land disputes.
SLB.entityNote: Incorporated society or charitable trust under local law; foreigners may participate; small registries.

ZWE.landNote: Agricultural land nationalised (2005); leases mainly for citizens; tenure insecure.
ZWE.fundingNote: 2025 PVO Amendment Act: scrutiny of funding sources, power to suspend boards and seize assets.

LBY.fundingNote: Foreign funding requires approval; NGOs targeted.

TJK.landNote: All land state-owned; foreigners only obtain limited use rights.
TJK.entityNote: Public associations tightly controlled; frequent liquidations.
TJK.fundingNote: Foreign funding must be registered with the state; heavy surveillance.

MWI.landNote: Land Act 2016: non-citizens leasehold only, for investment purposes.
MWI.entityNote: NGO Act (2022 amendment raised fees and penalties).
MWI.fundingNote: No explicit ban; NGO Authority oversight.

IRQ.landNote: Foreigners generally cannot own land (limited exceptions incl. Kurdistan Region).
IRQ.fundingNote: Foreign funds require approval; operational restrictions.

GIN.landNote: Land code allows private titles; foreigners need approvals.
GIN.entityNote: Association by declaration (French-style law); NGO status needs a ministry agreement; foreigners may found.

EGY.landNote: Foreigners barred from agricultural land (Law 15/1963); desert land via state; Sinai restricted.
EGY.fundingNote: Foreign funds need ministry approval; NGOs prosecuted (Case 173).

GNB.entityNote: Association by declaration (French-style law); NGO status needs a ministry agreement; foreigners may found.

BFA.landNote: Land tenure law restricts rural acquisition; insecurity.
BFA.entityNote: Junta has dissolved many associations since 2024.

NRU.landNote: Land owned by Nauruans; leases need Presidential consent; tiny island.
NRU.entityNote: Incorporated society or charitable trust under local law; foreigners may participate; small registries.

LBR.landNote: Constitution reserves land ownership to citizens; foreigners lease (up to ~50 years).

VEN.landNote: Foreigners may formally own land, but expropriations and agrarian law make tenure insecure.
VEN.entityNote: NGO registry under 2024 NGO law; arbitrary closures.
VEN.fundingNote: 2024 NGO oversight law requires disclosing funders; foreign funding treated as suspect.

DJI.landNote: Foreigners may hold land with approvals; much land state-owned.
DJI.fundingNote: Limited civic space; foreign funding monitored.

PNG.landNote: About 97% customary land; foreigners access via state lease-lease-back or ILG leases (up to 99 yrs), often contested.
PNG.entityNote: Association (Associations Incorporation Act) or company; foreigners may participate.

GMB.entityNote: NGO registration with NGO Affairs Agency.

MMR.landNote: 1987 law bars foreigners from owning land; civil war; leases only via investment approvals.
MMR.entityNote: 2022 Organization Registration Law criminalises unregistered groups.
MMR.fundingNote: Military regime controls all foreign funding.

NGA.landNote: Land Use Act: land under state governors; certificates of occupancy (99 yrs) need governor consent; foreigners via a Nigerian company.
NGA.entityNote: Incorporated trustees (CAC); foreigners may be trustees; CAMA 2020 lets regulator suspend trustees.
NGA.fundingNote: No explicit cap on foreign funding; periodic NGO-regulation bills.

COG.landNote: State domain dominates; foreigners need approvals.
COG.entityNote: Association by declaration (French-style law); NGO status needs a ministry agreement; foreigners may found.

PAK.landNote: Foreigners need Interior Ministry clearance; local entity route; security issues.
PAK.entityNote: Societies/trusts face security vetting; INGOs tightly regulated.
PAK.fundingNote: Local NGOs need EAD MoU/approval for foreign funds; INGOs expelled.

MRT.landNote: Land largely state/customary; foreigners via concessions.
MRT.entityNote: 2021 associations law moved to declaration regime.

SYR.landNote: Conflict-affected; foreign ownership requires approval; no secure tenure.

BDI.landNote: Land disputes widespread; foreigners need approvals.
BDI.fundingNote: Foreign funds must go through central bank and state oversight.

BGD.landNote: Foreigners need government approval; usually via a local company; land disputes common.
BGD.entityNote: Society or trust; NGO Affairs Bureau registration for foreign-funded work.
BGD.fundingNote: Foreign Donations Act 2016: each foreign-funded project needs NGOAB prior approval.

MOZ.landNote: All land state-owned; foreigners obtain DUAT use rights (up to 50 yrs renewable) via approved investment project.
MOZ.entityNote: Associação registration; newer NPO law tightened oversight.
MOZ.fundingNote: No explicit ban; increasing AML scrutiny.

TGO.landNote: Foreigners may acquire with approvals; customary land complex.
TGO.entityNote: Association by declaration (French-style law); NGO status needs a ministry agreement; foreigners may found.

AFG.landNote: Taliban rule; no secure tenure for foreigners.
AFG.entityNote: NGOs heavily restricted; women barred from NGO work.
AFG.fundingNote: Foreign funding tightly controlled by de facto authorities.

TCD.landNote: Land largely state/customary; foreigners via concessions.
TCD.entityNote: Association by declaration (French-style law); NGO status needs a ministry agreement; foreigners may found.

CMR.landNote: National-domain land; foreigners need approvals; titling slow.
CMR.entityNote: Associations by declaration; NGO status needs approval.
CMR.fundingNote: 2024: authorities ordered declarations/monitoring of foreign funds; suspensions.

AGO.landNote: All land originally state-owned; foreigners get surface rights via investment approvals.
AGO.entityNote: Associations need state recognition; restrictive NGO statute.

LSO.landNote: Land Act 2010: foreigners hold land title only via enterprises with Basotho participation.
LSO.entityNote: Society or company limited by guarantee.

MLI.fundingNote: Ban on French-funded NGOs (2022); heavy control.

YEM.fundingNote: Foreign funding heavily controlled by authorities.

COD.landNote: All land state-owned; foreigners get ordinary concessions (limited term); perpetual concessions for Congolese only.
COD.entityNote: ASBL needs Justice Ministry authorisation; slow.
COD.fundingNote: No explicit ban; insecurity and oversight.

CAF.entityNote: Association by declaration (French-style law); NGO status needs a ministry agreement; foreigners may found.

HTI.landNote: Constitution limits foreign ownership (one residence per district); weak titles; severe insecurity.
HTI.entityNote: NGO registration with planning ministry; weak state capacity.
HTI.fundingNote: No legal ban, but operating environment extremely insecure.

SDN.fundingNote: Foreign funding controlled; humanitarian access curtailed.

ERI.landNote: All land state-owned; no foreign tenure.

SSD.landNote: Land community-owned; foreigners lease only; conflict.
SSD.fundingNote: NGO Act limits admin spending; heavy oversight.

SOM.landNote: Fragile state; no secure land administration for foreigners.

_method: 0-100 sub-scores. land: freedom of a foreign-founded group to hold 50-2,000 ha rural land long-term (100 free freehold; 70 permit/caps; 40 local-majority entity or long lease; 15 short lease; 0 impossible). entity: ease of forming a nonprofit/co-op/foundation with foreign founders. funding: freedom to receive foreign donations. Scored from statutes and 2024-26 reports; est=true if unverified.
_sources: abogados.com.ar - Ley de Tierras Rurales / DNU 70/2023 status (2024-2026)
CIVICUS Monitor ratings (research/civicus_parsed.json) - cross-check for funding estimates
Background expert knowledge of national land/NGO statutes; ICNL Civic Freedom Monitor and World Bank Doing Business/B-READY used as general reference (not fetched per country)
